canDo: Can compare two options, avoid repetition with certains/d’autres/plusieurs and the like, and admit one drawback of the option chosen.
review: Review comparison and contrast; add common pronoms indéfinis.
input: Listening and reading about making choices.
output: Write a 150-word comparison of options; make a recommendation aloud in 3 minutes.
checkpoint: At least 3 criteria compared + 1 concession + a clear choice.
challenge: Today’s challenge: compare two neighbourhoods you know (or two commuting routes) in 6 sentences, using at least 3 of certains, d’autres, plusieurs, chacun; mark the contrast with alors que / en revanche, and admit one drawback of the option you choose.

questions.why: « Son inconvénient est ailleurs » — explicitly ruling out installation cost and radiator compatibility.
The regional grant only applies to new-build, so the real difference is about 3.4 million, not 5.6 million.
Building new takes 26 months, but the old building can partly stay open during the work; with a renovation it can’t.
After three or four years it loses about a third of its capacity, and replacing it costs about a quarter of the price of the bike.
The first speaker’s reason is that many children have never been to Paris.
Last year, six families couldn’t afford the Lyon trip, and six pupils stayed at school.
The last two options are precisely what characterises digital lending.

V24-01.exZh: The real question is: are you willing to arrive having worked up a sweat?

V24-02.zh: the advantage / the drawback is that …
V24-02.exZh: The drawback is that the battery loses a third of its capacity in four years.

V24-03.exZh: An ordinary bike costs a third as much; on the other hand, the hill will be hard.

V24-04.exZh: Compared with new, this refurbished one costs 40% less.

V24-05.exZh: A condensing gas boiler remains relevant in old buildings connected to the network.

V24-06.exZh: Paper dominates for children’s books, while digital is used mainly for new releases.

V24-07.zh: the strong point / the weak point
V24-07.exZh: Its weak point is the weight: twenty-five kilos.

V24-08.exZh: You shouldn’t compare the two gross amounts, which aren’t comparable.

V24-09.exZh: The nursery buys security at the cost of flexibility.

V24-10.exZh: With the grant, the price difference is no longer 5.6 million but about 3.4.

V24-11.exZh: Doing the opposite amounts to buying a solution before defining the problem.

V24-12.zh: to cost half / a third as much (as)
V24-12.exZh: An ordinary bike costs a third as much as an electric one.

V24-13.exZh: Building new costs 9.8 million — more than double.

V24-14.exZh: More and more things are rented by the month instead of being bought.

V24-15.exZh: A refurbished item only 15% cheaper than new is rarely a good deal.

V24-16.exZh: The deciding criterion isn’t the label, it’s the guarantee.

V24-17.exZh: Wood is the cheapest to run where supply is local.

V24-18.exZh: There’s no best heating, only a system suited to each home.

V24-19.zh: in absolute terms, in the abstract
V24-19.exZh: There’s no best heating in absolute terms.

V24-20.exZh: For seven flat kilometres, an ordinary bike is more than enough.

V24-21.exZh: Without a shower at work, an electric bike isn’t a luxury.

V24-22.exZh: It isn’t a deal-breaker, but you need to know before you buy.

V24-23.exZh: I understand the argument, but we need to look at who actually goes.

V24-24.exZh: When taking out a subscription, almost everyone underestimates how long they’ll use it.

V24-25.exZh: The neighbourhood is well served: two tram lines and a station.

V24-26.exZh: A heat pump is only efficient in a well-insulated home.

V24-27.exZh: Installed in a badly insulated home, a heat pump uses a lot of power.

V24-28.zh: to make do with, to work with …
V24-28.exZh: A gas boiler works with the existing radiators.

V24-29.exZh: Electric convector heaters are only justified in a very small home.

V24-30.zh: to settle for, to make do with …
V24-30.exZh: Some sellers settle for a clean and a quick test.

V24-31.exZh: A new product benefits from the legal guarantee for two years.

V24-32.exZh: Unless a hidden defect is proven, the buyer bears the risk.

V24-33.exZh: The seller undertakes to repair the appliance for a year.

V24-34.exZh: The council must decide between renovation and new-build before December.

V24-35.exZh: Three factors deserve to be weighed up before deciding.

V24-36.exZh: Digital lending hasn’t taken the place of paper lending: it has created a different use.

V24-37.exZh: A nanny share means getting on well with another family.

V24-38.exZh: We booked time off that we wouldn’t otherwise have taken.

V24-39.zh: to be paid by someone (cost borne by)
V24-39.exZh: With three day trips, families don’t have to pay anything.

V24-40.exZh: Below a certain threshold, subscribing is better value than buying.

V24-41.exZh: The idea of replacement misses what we actually observe.

V24-42.exZh: And in terms of the budget, what difference does it make?

V24-43.exZh: To get to work, I car-share with two colleagues.

V24-44.exZh: My commute is seven kilometres, including a steep hill.

V24-45.exZh: My 18:12 train was cancelled without notice.

title: Comparing options and weighing them up
